root_cause_label: Repeated %.2f Rounding Without Checking Expected Precision
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent correctly normalized heterogeneous date formats and computed the right average (11.429) but persistently used two-decimal formatting (%.2f), writing 11.43 instead of the required 11.429, and never recognized this precision mismatch as the cause of failure.
t_err_evidence: Step 6: First awk pipeline writes avg_temp.txt using 'printf "%.2f\n", avg' -- the agent arbitrarily chooses two-decimal precision without consulting any test specification, locking in the format-drift pattern that persists through the final output.
t_commit_evidence: Step 26: Final join-and-aggregate pipeline writes /app/avg_temp.txt with 'printf "%.2f\n", sum/count', producing 11.43; intermediate files are then deleted at step 28, making the incorrect output irreversible.
t_surface_evidence: Step 9: cat avg_temp.txt shows '5.00' -- the first observable wrong output (caused by date-matching bug in early script), which the agent later recognizes as incorrect in step 11.
trigger_explanation: The agent never consulted or inferred the expected output precision from any task specification or test oracle; it assumed two-decimal rounding (%.2f) was appropriate at step 6, and this assumption was never revisited even after multiple reworkings of the pipeline.
forewarning_evidence: Step 9 shows '5.00' as output (obviously wrong given 7 data pairs); step 11 the agent manually computes 11.43 and recognizes the mismatch, but fixes only the date-normalization bug and never addresses the precision format issue before t_commit at step 26.
